newsitem.title: UK: SNOOKER-PARROTT FORCED TO FIGHT FOR QUARTER-FINAL SPOT.
newsitem.headline: SNOOKER-PARROTT FORCED TO FIGHT FOR QUARTER-FINAL SPOT.

text.p: Former title-holder John Parrott was forced to battle hard before beating qualifier Anthony Hamilton 13-11 to reach the world snooker championship quarter-finals for the eighth time in nine years on Monday.
Parrott, winner in 1991, had recovered from initially going 4-0 down in the opening frames on Sunday to begin the day 9-7 ahead of his fellow Englishman.
But the 25-year-old Hamilton, who beat veteran Jimmy White in the first round, fought his way back to level at 11-all after beginning the day with a break of 121 in the opening frame.
Parrott took the next two to open up a three-frame lead before Hamilton again fought back by winning the next three, including a break of 129, to draw level.
The former champion responded with the highest break of the match, a 133, to regain the lead and clinched the match comfortably by winning the next.
Hamilton can at least take comfort from the fact he has done enough to ensure a top 16 ranking for next season.

World number two John Higgins of Scotland had a much easier task as he saw off Welsh qualifier Dominic Dale to earn a quarter-final match against Irishman Ken Doherty who comprehensively defeated six-times former champion Steve Davis on Sunday.
Leading 6-2 overnight, Higgins never allowed his opponent back into the match and won 13-5.
